title: Verify Invariant: In add_to_bloom, the bit_to_set value MUST always be in range [0, 2047]

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The function add_to_bloom is an EVM Ethereum execution layer (EL) function that computes bloom filter bit positions from log topics and contract addresses. Prysm (the consensus layer client) does not implement add_to_bloom or any bloom filter bit computation. Prysm receives the LogsBloom field as a completed 256-byte opaque blob inside execution payloads from the EL client via the Engine API. The only state variable Prysm tracks related to LogsBloom is the raw byte slice field in execution payload proto structs. SSZ serialization code in proto/engine/v1/engine.ssz.go enforces a strict length check (size != 256) but does no bit-level validity checking whatsoever.
state_anomalies_found: No add_to_bloom implementation exists in Prysm; bloom filter bit computation (including bit_to_set derivation) is outside Prysm's trust boundary
Prysm's SSZ layer validates LogsBloom byte count (must be exactly 256), but performs zero bit-level invariant checking — an EL client could theoretically produce a bloom with any bit pattern
No cross-layer validation: Prysm trusts the EL's computation of LogsBloom without independent verification of the bloom's semantic correctness
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: LogsBloom is stored as an immutable field in execution payload protobuf structs. Once deserialized from the Engine API response, it is passed through Prysm unchanged. No bloom-related caching or state mutation occurs in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrent access concerns exist in Prysm for this field. The LogsBloom blob is treated as a read-only value after deserialization.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Because add_to_bloom does not exist in Prysm, there is no code path in Prysm where an attacker could trigger an out-of-range bit_to_set value through Prysm's own logic. All symbolic execution paths through Prysm related to LogsBloom lead only to the SSZ length check (size == 256). The bloom filter semantic invariant (bit_to_set in [0, 2047], byte_index in [0, 255]) is entirely the responsibility of the EL client that produces the payload.
attack_scenarios: A malicious or buggy EL client could produce a LogsBloom with any byte content; Prysm would accept it as long as it is exactly 256 bytes — however this is by design and outside Prysm's audit scope
No path exists in Prysm itself to produce a bloom filter with an invalid bit_to_set value
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependencies. The invariant in question is not implemented in Prysm at all.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The add_to_bloom function and the bit_to_set invariant are entirely absent from Prysm's codebase. No Prysm code path implements bloom filter bit computation. The EL client is the sole implementer of this logic, accessed through the Engine API (newPayload). Prysm has no code to audit for this invariant.
entry_points: Engine API (newPayload) response from EL client — LogsBloom is accepted as an opaque 256-byte blob
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No attack surface exists within Prysm for this invariant. The EL client (e.g., go-ethereum) is responsible for bloom filter correctness, and Prysm enforces only byte-length integrity.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'bit_to_set in [0, 2047]' is not a Prysm invariant. Prysm's only applicable invariant for LogsBloom is length equality to 256 bytes, which is enforced by SSZ serialization code in proto/engine/v1/engine.ssz.go at line 582 ('if size := len(e.LogsBloom); size != 256'). This length check is sufficient for Prysm's purpose but irrelevant to the EL-level bloom computation invariant being audited.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ byte-length check: `if size := len(e.LogsBloom); size != 256` in /target_workspace/proto/engine/v1/engine.ssz.go:582
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: The guard is sufficient for Prysm's scope (structural blob integrity). It is irrelevant to the semantic invariant (bit_to_set in [0, 2047]) which belongs to the EL layer. Prysm correctly delegates bloom computation to the EL.
edge_cases: LogsBloom field accepted from builder API (MEV-boost) also undergoes the same 256-byte length check via fieldparams.LogsBloomLength constant
No edge case exists where Prysm could produce an invalid bit_to_set value since Prysm does not compute bloom filters

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The function add_to_bloom and the invariant bit_to_set in [0, 2047] do not exist in Prysm. This check was generated from EL-layer specifications (EVM yellow paper / go-ethereum) but applied to the wrong audit target. Prysm is a consensus layer client that treats LogsBloom as an opaque 256-byte blob validated solely by length. There is no code path in Prysm to exploit or test for this invariant.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: This check should be redirected to the EL client audit (e.g., go-ethereum / Nitro). No action required in Prysm.

title: Verify Invariant: In add_to_bloom, the byte_index MUST always be in range [0, 255]

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Like bit_to_set, the byte_index invariant for add_to_bloom is an EL-layer concern. In the EVM specification, byte_index is derived as bit_to_set >> 3 where bit_to_set is in [0, 2047], mathematically guaranteeing byte_index in [0, 255]. Prysm has no implementation of add_to_bloom and no code that computes byte_index. The LogsBloom field in Prysm is a 256-byte blob received from the EL and validated only for length correctness (via SSZ and fieldparams.LogsBloomLength = 256).
state_anomalies_found: No byte_index computation exists anywhere in Prysm; this is an EL-exclusive invariant
LogsBloom is stored as []byte in execution payload proto; Prysm enforces only len == 256
No Prysm code indexes into LogsBloom by bit position or computed byte index
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Same as CHK-PROP-W5B6-41-001. LogsBloom is immutable after Engine API deserialization. No bloom caching or mutation in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrency issues. LogsBloom bytes are read-only after assignment from Engine API response.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: With no add_to_bloom in Prysm, the symbolic execution space for this invariant is empty within Prysm's codebase. Any symbolic analysis of byte_index must target the EL client. No counterexample can be constructed within Prysm's code because the invariant's code does not exist there.
attack_scenarios: No exploitable path exists in Prysm for byte_index going out of range [0, 255]
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Not applicable — no relevant code in Prysm.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The byte_index computation is completely absent from Prysm. The only LogsBloom-related code in Prysm is (1) SSZ length validation, (2) hex encoding/decoding for REST API, and (3) proto field storage. None of these involve byte_index computation.
entry_points: Engine API newPayload response (LogsBloom field as opaque blob)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No attack surface in Prysm for this invariant. EL client exclusively implements byte_index derivation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The byte_index invariant is mathematically guaranteed by the EL specification (byte_index = bit_to_set >> 3, bit_to_set in [0,2047] => byte_index in [0,255]). Prysm neither implements this computation nor needs to validate it, as it trusts the EL's output. Prysm's only relevant constraint — len(LogsBloom) == 256 — is proven correct by SSZ code.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ byte-length check: `if size := len(e.LogsBloom); size != 256` in /target_workspace/proto/engine/v1/engine.ssz.go:582
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for Prysm's scope. The byte_index invariant is not Prysm's responsibility.
edge_cases: No edge cases apply within Prysm for this invariant

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: add_to_bloom and byte_index computation do not exist in Prysm. The invariant is an EL-exclusive concern. Prysm correctly enforces only structural (length) validity of the LogsBloom blob received from the EL. This check is out of scope for the Prysm consensus layer audit.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Redirect to EL client audit. No changes needed in Prysm.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the GAS_CAP constant exactly 16777216 (2^24) in all code paths?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: GAS_CAP = 16777216 (2^24) is a txpool-level constant used in execution layer clients (e.g., go-ethereum) to cap individual transaction gas limits in the transaction pool. Prysm, as a consensus layer client, has no txpool and does not implement GAS_CAP. The only occurrence of 16777216 in Prysm's non-test code is HistoricalRootsLength (HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT = 2^24), which is an entirely unrelated beacon chain state parameter. DefaultBuilderGasLimit in Prysm (30-60M) is a different concept — it is a suggested gas limit sent to MEV-boost builders for block production, not a per-transaction cap.
state_anomalies_found: No GAS_CAP constant or EL txpool gas capping logic exists in Prysm
HistoricalRootsLength = 16777216 is correctly used for SSZ list size limits (HistoricalRoots and HistoricalSummaries in beacon state) — this is the correct and expected usage
DefaultBuilderGasLimit (30-60M range depending on testnet/mainnet) is unrelated to GAS_CAP and is the maximum gas for an entire block, not per transaction
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: The HistoricalRootsLength constant is used in SSZ marshaling/unmarshaling for beacon state historical roots lists. No caching concerns for a constant value. The constant is defined at compile time and cannot be mutated.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrency concerns. Constants are immutable by definition.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: There is no code path in Prysm where a GAS_CAP = 16777216 check occurs on transaction data. The builder gas limit (DefaultBuilderGasLimit) is set per network configuration and is a suggested limit sent to external builders. The HistoricalRootsLength SSZ limit is applied consistently across all SSZ encode/decode paths for the beacon state field. No exploit scenario exists for GAS_CAP in Prysm because the concept does not apply.
attack_scenarios: An attacker cannot exploit a non-existent GAS_CAP implementation in Prysm
The HistoricalRootsLength = 16777216 usage in SSZ is arithmetically correct and consistently applied
DefaultBuilderGasLimit misconfiguration between testnet (60M) and mainnet (45M) is a separate concern not related to GAS_CAP

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: GAS_CAP as a txpool per-transaction gas limit concept is unreachable in Prysm. Prysm does not process individual EL transactions and has no code that would apply or skip a GAS_CAP check. The closest concept — DefaultBuilderGasLimit — is a block-level parameter sent outbound to external MEV-boost builders, not a validation constraint on incoming transactions.
entry_points: Engine API (newPayload, getPayload) — no per-transaction gas capping occurs in Prysm
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No attack surface within Prysm. GAS_CAP is an EL txpool concept exclusively.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'GAS_CAP = 16777216 in all code paths' does not apply to Prysm. The only verification relevant is that HistoricalRootsLength = 16777216 is correctly used as the SSZ list limit for HistoricalRoots and HistoricalSummaries fields — which is confirmed correct in proto/prysm/v1alpha1/fulu.ssz.go and phase0.ssz.go. This constant is the right value for HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT per the Ethereum consensus spec.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SSZ list size limit check: `if size := len(b.HistoricalRoots); size > 16777216` in /target_workspace/proto/prysm/v1alpha1/fulu.ssz.go:1023 (correctly guards HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT, not GAS_CAP)
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: The guard is correct and sufficient for its actual purpose (beacon state historical roots SSZ limit). The concept of GAS_CAP does not exist in Prysm.
edge_cases: Testnet DefaultBuilderGasLimit (60M) vs mainnet (45M) is intentional per network config and not a security issue
No edge case where 16777216 is incorrectly used as GAS_CAP was found

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: GAS_CAP = 16777216 as a txpool per-transaction gas limit is an EL concept entirely absent from Prysm. The number 16777216 appears in Prysm only as HISTORICAL_ROOTS_LIMIT (a beacon chain state parameter), which is correct and unrelated. Prysm delegates transaction validation to the EL client. This check is fundamentally misscoped against Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Redirect to EL client (go-ethereum/Nitro) audit for GAS_CAP txpool enforcement. Confirm HistoricalRootsLength usage in Prysm is correct (it is). No Prysm changes needed.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does txpool reject transactions with gasLimit > 16777216?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm has no txpool implementation whatsoever. Transaction pool management — including any per-transaction gasLimit validation — is exclusively the responsibility of the EL client (e.g., go-ethereum, Nitro). Prysm interacts with the EL only via the Engine API (forkchoiceUpdated, newPayload, getPayload), which operates at the block granularity, not the individual transaction level. No file in the Prysm main codebase (outside end-to-end test infrastructure referencing external geth/Nitro nodes) contains txpool or TransactionPool.
state_anomalies_found: No txpool implementation in Prysm — confirmed by exhaustive search finding only external geth references in testing infrastructure (testing/endtoend/components/eth1/)
Prysm passes entire execution payloads (with transactions as opaque byte slices) to/from the EL; it never inspects individual transaction gas limits
GasLimit field in execution payload structs (block-level, not transaction-level) is accepted without a hard cap check in Prysm — but this is block gas limit, not per-transaction cap
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No txpool cache or state exists in Prysm. The GasLimit field in ExecutionPayload (block-level) is stored as uint64 in the proto struct and validated only via SSZ uint64 marshaling (no range check beyond uint64 limits).
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable — no txpool state to have concurrency issues on.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: With no txpool in Prysm, symbolic execution of 'does Prysm reject gasLimit > 16777216 transactions' yields a trivially empty path set. There is no branch in Prysm code that reads individual transaction gasLimit values. The execution payload's block-level GasLimit is passed through unchanged via the Engine API. No symbolic path leads to a gasLimit check against 16777216.
attack_scenarios: No attack scenario exists in Prysm for missing per-transaction gasLimit validation
An attacker submitting transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 would interact with the EL client's txpool, not Prysm

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Per-transaction gasLimit validation is completely unreachable within Prysm. Prysm's Engine API client (beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go) sends and receives execution payloads containing the full serialized transaction list as opaque bytes. Prysm never deserializes individual transactions to check their gasLimit fields.
entry_points: Engine API newPayload (block-level, not transaction-level validation)
Builder API (getPayload from MEV-boost) — block-level GasLimit only
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Zero attack surface in Prysm for txpool gasLimit enforcement. The EL client exclusively owns this responsibility.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'txpool rejects gasLimit > 16777216' is not implemented and not intended to be implemented in Prysm. The block-level GasLimit field in ExecutionPayload structs flows through Prysm without per-transaction gasLimit constraint checking, which is architecturally correct for a consensus layer client. SSZ validates GasLimit as a uint64 (type safety only, no upper bound beyond uint64 max).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: No guard for this invariant in Prysm — correct by design as txpool is an EL concern
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Not applicable to Prysm. The EL client is the responsible party.
edge_cases: Block-level GasLimit in execution payloads is not range-checked by Prysm; an EL client could theoretically provide a block with GasLimit exceeding expected values, but this would be caught by EL-layer validation upon newPayload call

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: txpool and per-transaction gasLimit enforcement do not exist in Prysm by design. The consensus layer client's responsibility is block-level validity via state transition, not mempool transaction filtering. This check is explicitly out of scope for a Prysm audit.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Redirect to EL client audit. No Prysm changes required.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does P2P-relayed transaction validation match local validation?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm's P2P layer (based on libp2p) handles consensus layer gossip topics exclusively: beacon blocks, attestations, sync committee messages, BLS-to-execution-change messages, voluntary exits, proposer/attester slashings, blob sidecars, and data column sidecars. No EL transaction gossip topic is handled by Prysm. EL transaction gossip (eth/68 protocol, devp2p) is exclusively the domain of the EL client. The beacon-chain/sync/ package contains no transaction validation handlers; all handlers deal with consensus objects (blocks, attestations, etc.).
state_anomalies_found: Prysm implements zero EL transaction P2P gossip handling — confirmed by enumeration of all subscriber_*.go and validate_*.go files in beacon-chain/sync/
Prysm does maintain a peer ID to node ID conversion utility (ConvertPeerIDToNodeID in beacon-chain/p2p/utils.go) for libp2p/devp2p bridging, but this is purely metadata, not transaction relaying
No validate_transaction.go or subscriber_transaction.go files exist in Prysm
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No transaction P2P state, caches, or queues exist in Prysm. Beacon gossip caches (e.g., seen block roots, attestation dedup) are exclusively for consensus objects.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable — no transaction P2P handling to have concurrency issues on.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Since Prysm has no code that handles P2P-relayed EL transactions, there is no code path where a discrepancy between P2P-relayed validation and local validation could occur within Prysm. All EL transaction P2P validation is handled by the EL client. The symbolic execution space for this invariant within Prysm is empty.
attack_scenarios: An attacker attempting to exploit P2P vs local validation inconsistency for EL transactions would need to target the EL client's devp2p implementation, not Prysm
Prysm's libp2p gossip handles only consensus layer objects; no transaction validation asymmetry can exist in Prysm
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: None — no transaction P2P handling in Prysm.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: EL transaction P2P gossip is unreachable within Prysm's codebase. The devp2p network (eth/68 protocol) carrying EL transactions is managed entirely by the EL client. Prysm's libp2p network carries only consensus layer gossip (attestations, blocks, etc.). These are completely separate network stacks with no intersection in Prysm's code.
entry_points: Prysm P2P: libp2p — handles beacon blocks, attestations, sync committee msgs, BLS-to-execution-change, blob sidecars (NO transaction gossip)
EL P2P: devp2p eth/68 — handles transaction gossip (outside Prysm, in EL client)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Zero attack surface in Prysm for transaction P2P validation asymmetry. The EL client exclusively owns transaction gossip and validation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'P2P-relayed transaction validation matches local validation' is structurally inapplicable to Prysm. Prysm neither relays EL transactions via P2P nor performs local EL transaction validation. The separation of concerns (CL libp2p for consensus gossip, EL devp2p for transaction gossip) is architecturally fundamental to the Ethereum post-merge design. Prysm's implementation of this separation is correct and complete.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Architectural separation: Prysm's sync package contains no transaction subscriber or validator (beacon-chain/sync/ enumeration confirms only consensus object handlers exist)
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: The architectural separation is sufficient and correct. No transaction validation code exists in Prysm to have asymmetry in.
edge_cases: Prysm's ConvertPeerIDToNodeID utility for libp2p/devp2p ID conversion is metadata-only and creates no transaction validation surface

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: EL transaction P2P gossip and validation is entirely outside Prysm's scope. Prysm is a consensus layer client that uses libp2p exclusively for consensus layer gossip. EL transaction propagation uses a completely separate devp2p network stack managed by the EL client. The invariant being checked (P2P tx validation parity) does not apply to Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Redirect to EL client audit (go-ethereum/Nitro eth/68 protocol handler). No Prysm changes required.
